MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  JULY 6, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  —

  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:03 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Doug Stewart; Commissioners Daphne Anneet,
  and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ABSENT:  Commissioner Keegan Gibbs

  ALSO PRESENT:  Steve McClary, City Manager; Susan Dueflas, Public Safety
  Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Sarah
  Kaplan, Emergency Services Coordinator; Brad Yocum, Fire Safety Liaison; Gabe
  Etcheverry, Fire Safety Liaison; Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant; Parker
  Davis, Media Technician; Lieutenant Chad Watters, Los Angeles County Sheriffs
  Department; and Mary Linden, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Fire Safety Liaison Yocum led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Chair Frost moved and Commissioner Anneet seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner Gibbs
  absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on June 29, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL / PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Lloyd Ahern, President of Las Tunas Homeowners Association (HOA), stated the
  City had an unsafe Fourth of July holiday. He discussed a person who attacked
  several homes on July 3 and July 4 with an axe. He commended the Sheriffs
  Department for its response. He stated he would meet with City staff tomorrow. He
  discussed fear in his community. He stated it was critical to catch the man before

  Ryan Embree discussed the Sheriffs tower at 23555 Civic Center Way. He stated
  it should not be classified as an emergency device.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Director Dueflas reported the City Council directed staff to prepare
  two Requests for Proposals (RFP) for school safety, including a comprehensive
  assessment of security at schools, and for security personnel to be added at school
  sites. She stated staff was meeting with the Council’s ad hoc committee and school
  district representatives tomorrow. She stated there was another meeting tomorrow
  regarding installation of a KBUU antenna on the Michael Landon Center. She
  introduced Brad Yocum, one of the City’s two new Fire Safety Liaisons.

  Fire Safety Liaison Yocum discussed his experience with the Los Angeles County
  Fire Department, including brush clearance, fuel modification, and home
  hardening.

  Public Safety Director Dueñas discussed Public Safety changes with the adoption
  of the Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Budget. She announced Public Safety was now an
  official department in the City, and Sarah Kaplan was promoted to Emergency
  Services Coordinator. She commended Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan
  for a well-deserved promotion. In response to Mr. Ahern, she confirmed staff and
  the Sheriffs Department would meet with Las Tunas residents tomorrow.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores discussed an overnight parking operation last week to
  observe parking violation issues. He stated Las Tunas Beach had a higher
  concentration of recreational vehicles (RV) parked overnight. He stated
  approximately one-quarter of RVs appeared to be irthabited by homeless
  individuals. He stated the homeless count numbers should be released later this
  month. He announced a Homeless Connect Day was tentatively scheduled for
  September 22.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry discussed a small fire on Latigo Canyon today. He
  stated the cause was unknown, but it was determined that it did not involve a
  homeless encampment.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated 84 vehicles had been towed to the temporary
  impound yard since June 18.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated the last reported live fuel moisture level was
  74 on June 23, which was in line with last year. He stated the National Weather
  Service (NWS) recently provided an updated forecast of a third consecutive La
  Nina event next winter. He suggested adding discussion of other measures that
  indicate fire threat to the agenda for a future meeting.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated maintenance crews worked the holiday
  weekend with no major incidents to report. He stated City staff coordinated with
  the Los Angeles County Department of Beaches and Harbors prior to the holiday
  to discuss strategies for improving parking at Zuma Beach. He announced Caltrans
  was terminating its project to install a pedestrian hybrid beacon on Pacific Coast
  Highway (PCH) near Malibu Seafood.

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Vice Chair Stewart discussed a recent power outage in eastern Malibu. He stated
  backup batteries on traffic signals did not provide four hours of power. Public
  Works Director DuBoux stated he was working with Caltrans so the backup
  batteries worked during unscheduled power outages.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth congratulated Public Safety Director Dueñas on
  her new role as department director. He discussed the need for wrapping and
  retrofitting wooden poles, particularly along evacuation routes. He discussed a car
  fire on Stunt Road. He stated he discussed community fire brigades with the Hidden
  Hills City Manager. He stated home ignition zone assessments were being
  conducted. He discussed a fire on Piuma Road on July 4.

  Commissioner Anneet thanked everyone for keeping the beach safe over the
  holiday weekend. She discussed parking citations. She asked about the purpose of
  citing visitors for expired registration tabs.

  In response to Ex Officio Member Woodworth, Commissioner Spiegel stated Todd
  Prince, Malibu Arson Watch, advised him that one of 71 Arson Watch patrols had
  called in the fire on Piuma Road using its new radios. He commended Mr. Prince
  and the members of Arson Watch for providing a good presence in the mountains.
  He discussed his ride-along with Deputy Menejyan. He stated it was very
  informative. He recommended all commissioners do a ride-along. He stated he
  attended the Public Safety Expo, which was well-organized. He expressed
  disappointment it was not more widely attended. He suggested trying a different
  venue. He stated Mark Russo, Volunteers on Patrol (VOP), indicated the fourth
  VOP car was ready but unavailable due to unfinished County bailment agreement

  paperwork. He requested the City put pressure on the County to put it on an
  upcoming Board of Supervisors agenda.

  Public Safety Director Dueflas stated a County representative was looking into what
  was delaying approval of the bailment agreement.

  In response to Commissioner Spiegel, Public Safety Director Dueñas stated the
  budget approved the City Council for the license plate readers was less than the
  actual cost. She stated the request to Council was based on an estimate from the
  supplier. She stated she was working with the Interim City Attorney to resolve the
  issues.

  In response to Commissioner Spiegel, Public Safety Director Dueñas stated she was
  looking into when the stairs at Big Dume would be opened. Commissioner Spiegel
  congratulated Chair Frost on his recent wedding.

  Vice Chair Stewart stated the CERT team worked the Public Safety Expo, the Point
  Dume Fourth of July parade, and was helping with CERT training. He discussed a
  rise in crime. He discussed the size of the KBUU antenna to be installed. He
  discussed backup generators for water pumps in Big Rock. He asked about the
  status of brush clearance inspections.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated the City did not tally jurisdictional fire station
  progress. He stated the County’s Agriculture and Fire Departments were doing
  inspections. He stated City staff responded to resident questions about certain
  properties and then notified the appropriate County office. In response to Vice
  Chair Stewart, Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated questions were better directed
  directly to the jurisdictional fire station for properties with structures or County
  Agriculture if the property had no structures. In response to Vice Chair Stewart,
  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed the process for installing speed limit
  signs where speed limits were reduced.

  Chair Frost discussed thefis off poles in the canyons, most likely taking copper
  wire. He stated it may be the cause of some recent power outages. He commended
  Lieutenant Watters for clearing so many illegally parked vehicles on PCH. He
  expressed frustration with delays in approving the bailment agreement for the
  fourth VOP car. He discussed maintenance needed for signs in Las Tunas. He
  discussed new mobile vendors selling in Malibu without the appropriate permits
  and licenses. He agreed with Commissioner Spiegel in commending Arson Watch
  for reporting and assisting with the fire over the weekend. He discussed the
  apparent turnover of individuals experiencing homelessness. He discussed
  problems accessing Westward Beach.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item No. 3 .B.1. was pulled by the public.

  Ryan Embree stated his comments at the May 4, 2022 meeting about the pole at
  23555 Civic Center Way were made for the record and should be included in the
  minutes. He stated the pole is not an emergency facility but operates daily and has
  a cellphone component, that it is a different facility than the previous tower, and
  that the colocation appears to be expanded. He stated changes were made without
  noticing. He encouraged the Commission to have a Fire Department representative
  attend its meetings. He asked how many vehicles were towed from Malibu to
  Oxnard. He stated fire hydrants were not being actively flow-tested. He asked how
  many automated license plate reader (ALPR) cars were operating.

  Executive Assistant Linden clarified that staff provided summary minutes.

MOTION  Vice Chair Stewart moved and Commissioner Spiegel seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-
  0, Commissioner Gibbs absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes May 4, 2022
  —

  Staff recommendation: Approve minutes of the Public Safety Commission
  Regular meeting of May 4, 2022.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Sheriff Access to Gated Communities
  Recommended Action: 1) Review options for providing Los Angeles County
  Sheriff’s Deputies access to gated communities through the installation of
  emergency key systems; and 2) Provide a recommendation to the City Council to
  implement the preferred option, if appropriate.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores presented the report. He introduced Lost Hills Station
  (LHS) Deputy Brian Knott who oversees emergency access systems in Calabasas.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of July 6, 2022
Page 6 of 8

  Deputy Knott stated the Calabasas program was for unmanned, gated communities.
  He stated Westlake Village HOAs also agreed to install Knox boxes. He discussed
  the cost, which was paid for by the communities. He stated keys were provided
  only to Sheriff deputies, and Sheriff and Fire Department access keys were not
  interchangeable. He stated he receives inquiries from individual homeowners in
  Malibu. He stated the company was sending him test boxes to try before
  recommending them to Malibu.

  Vice Chair Stewart thanked Deputy Knott for attending. He stated some City
  Councilmembers did not want the Sheriffs Department to have access. He
  expressed support for installing the boxes. He suggested starting without an
  ordinance. He stated some homes within gated communities also had private gates.

  Ryan Embree discussed problems coordinating with HOAs. He stated it was
  important to obtain or renew trespassing signage that goes with Letters of Agency.
  He stated installation by certified installers was required. He discussed the cost for
  installing the boxes and electric gates. He suggested delaying an ordinance. He
  complimented Emergency Services Coordinator Kaplan on her promotion.

  Deputy Knott stated the cost for a box was under $1,000. He stated he issued keys
  to the deputies.

  Commissioner Anneet suggested beginning with a voluntary program.

  Deputy Knott discussed the process for a homeowner to purchase a box. He stated
  the supplier would contact LHS to complete the installation. He offered to assist
  with outreach through the LHS social media network.

  Commissioner Spiegel stated many HOAs did not have formal processes. He
  suggested the City conduct a robust campaign for voluntary participation.

MOTION  Vice Chair Stewart moved and Commissioner Anneet seconded a motion to provide
  a recommendation that: 1) the City conduct a community education campaign in
  support of a voluntary program for use of Knox box keys utilized by Lost Hills
  Sheriffs Station to provide Sheriffs Department emergency access to gated
  communities and gated properties; and 2) direct the Public Safety Commission to
  review the progress of the program after one year. The question was called, and the
  motion carried 4-0, Commissioner Gibbs absent.

  B.  Public Safety Agency Activity
  Recommended Action: Discuss recent Public Safety Agency activities and receive
  and file activity reports from the County of Los Angeles Sheriffs Department, Fire
  Department, and Lifeguard Division.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission

  Lieutenant Watters thanked Deputy Knott for his report on the Knox boxes. He
  discussed crimes and statistics in the Sheriffs Department’s report. He stated the
  Beach Team had issued 379 citations for alcohol on the beaches and over 2,000
  parking citations. He stated 109 vehicles had been towed for illegal parking causing
  a public safety concern. He commended the City for approving the temporary tow
  yard, which was working very well. He stated the suspect in the axe attack
  described by Mr. Ahern was known to the Sheriffs Department, and they expected
  to have him in custody soon. He discussed work of the Sheriffs Department’s
  Homeless Outreach Services Team (HOST) in Malibu at no cost to the City. He
  stated cooperation from shopping center owners discouraged car shows in their
  parking lots. He stated operations would be conducted to cite speeding and noise
  and exhaust from modified vehicles. He stated 37 vehicles were towed on July 4 to
  the temporary tow lot. He stated he spoke with Public Works Director DuBoux
  about unpermitted vendors and where permitted vendors were allowed to sell.

  In response to Commissioner Anneet, Lieutenant Watters stated deputies cited any
  violations of the vehicle or penal codes, including expired vehicle registration.

  Chair Frost stated many vehicles had tabs or license plates that did not belong to
  the vehicle.

  Commissioner Anneet lefi the meeting at 6:32 p.m.

  Ryan Embree asked if any vehicles were towed out of the City. He stated the MTA
  bus was a getaway vehicle for criminals. He asked if the duration of Letters of
  Agency could be extended to two years. He asked how many ALPR cars were in
  Malibu. He asked if overdue rental cars were included in the ALPR database.

  In response to Mr. Embree, Chair Frost stated there was an ALPR on one Sheriff
  vehicle in Malibu.

  Lieutenant Watters stated the Sheriffs Department communicated with MTA when
  necessary. He stated no vehicles had yet to be towed to Thousand Oaks.

  adjourn. The question was called, and the motion carried 3-0, Commissioner
